scope: Explicit historical maintenance only; no startup execution, automatic migration, production call or default apply. Supports an existing local SQLite file or verified-TLS PostgreSQL through the existing OpenPostgres policy; remote libSQL is rejected. CLI never creates or migrates a database.

Dry-run default emits counts, independent keyset cursors, source digest and credential-free target digest without requester names, URLs, raw queue JSON, export payloads, receipt results or connection secrets. Each table batch is 1-100 rows, each queue at most 201 entries and 2 MiB, and total reviewed payload bytes at most 64 MiB; oversized/corrupt data fails rather than truncating.

Apply requires a reviewed dry-run plan for identical target/cursors/limit/source and explicit --offline-confirmed acknowledgement after stopping application writes and taking a protected backup. The tool does not independently prove that writes are stopped. Every later batch requires separate review; no auto-loop is provided.

Batch transaction shares the existing retirement lock, recomputes the source and desired-change fingerprint, checks exact rows and rolls back on mismatch or error. Changed revisions, identity status, payloads or target invalidate the plan.

Only cached requester names linked to users.deleted_at tombstones become Deleted User. Existing RawMessage-preserving sanitizer retains stable IDs, queue order, media, duplicate entries, unknown fields and exact large numbers. Only queue_json is updated; head/session/revision/repeat/updated_at are preserved.

Only retired actors operation receipts and retired users export snapshots are removed. Null export payloads use a portable null-safe exact comparison. Live actors records and shared history are untouched.

postgres.fixture: Random password only in process environment; owned uniquely named loopback container, dynamic port, existing native migration/isolation harness. Exact owned container removed and prior environment restored. No credentials printed or saved.

linux_race.command: docker run --rm <read-only server bind and cached Go module/build volumes> -e CGO_ENABLED=1 golang:1.26.10-bookworm go test ./cmd/backfill-music-privacy ./repository -run 'TestBackfillCLI|TestMusicPrivacyBackfill' -race -count=1 -timeout=4m

scenarios: Dry-run changes no application rows and reports no private payloads
Distinct queue/receipt/export keysets and explicit subsequent batches
Unknown nested JSON and exact large numeric values retained
Control metadata/timestamps, live actors rows and duplicate media preserved
Revision, identity and target changes reject stale plans
Malformed batch cannot partially rewrite or delete records
Injected second queue update failure rolls back earlier update and deletions
Held retirement lock prevents acknowledgment until released, including actual pooled PostgreSQL
Nullable export CAS parity on SQLite and PostgreSQL
CLI refuses implicit apply, changed reviewed limit, wrong target, missing SQLite file and unsupported remote source

usage.configuration: HICHAT_MUSIC_PRIVACY_DATABASE_URL must be supplied through the local process environment; no credentials on command arguments or in reports.

remaining: Historical production at-rest cleanup remains pending explicit operator execution on a protected backup/offline production database. No production counts or completion claim exist.
PostgreSQL repository behavior was tested against a disposable local database; the CLI verified-TLS opener reuses existing policy. No production TLS/network connection was made for this command.
External/pre-maintenance backups are not erased by the tool; restoring them restores old private values and remains a separate operational/retention responsibility.
No broad repository rerun, whole-server CI, browser/device acceptance, commit, push or production publication was performed for this maintenance slice.
